questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈2.2778,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{12}, & 0<x<2, \\ \frac{7}{9}, & 2\le x<3, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{12}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{7}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{4}}{12}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{7{x}^{2}}{9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{5}}{60}|}_{0}^{2}+{\frac{7{x}^{3}}{27}|}_{2}^{3} \\  & ≈5.4593\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈5.4593-(2.2778)^{2} \\  & ≈0.271\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to three decimal places.

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(-\frac{4}{3{x}^{3}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\frac{4}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}})|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =2-{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈3.314\,81,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{9}, & 0<x<3, \\ \frac{1}{9}(2x-5), & 3\le x<5, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{9}(2x-5)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{5}\frac{1}{9}(2{x}^{3}-5{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{27}|}_{0}^{3}+{\frac{1}{9}(\frac{{x}^{4}}{2}-\frac{5{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{3}^{5} \\  & ≈13.074\,07\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈13.074\,07-(3.314\,81)^{2} \\  & ≈2.09\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈1.136\,90,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}x, & 0\le x<1, \\ \frac{3{x}^{2}}{14}, & 1\le x<2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{3{x}^{2}}{14}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{3{x}^{4}}{14}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{3{x}^{5}}{70}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =1.578\,57\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈1.578\,57-(1.136\,90)^{2} \\  & ≈0.29\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.

questions.problem:
Given that $X$ is a continuous random variable with the following probability density function, compute $\text{Var}[X].$ 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{30(x-1)}{{x}^{7}},\, & x\ge 1, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

First, we compute $\text{E}[X]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }x\cdot \frac{30(x-1)}{{x}^{7}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{30x-30}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{30}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{30}{{x}^{6}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{30}{4{x}^{4}}+\frac{30}{5{x}^{5}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =-\frac{15}{2{x}^{4}}+\frac{6}{{x}^{5}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{30(x-1)}{{x}^{7}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{30x-30}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{30}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{30}{{x}^{5}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{30}{3{x}^{3}}+\frac{30}{4{x}^{4}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =-\frac{10}{{x}^{3}}+\frac{15}{2{x}^{4}}{|}_{1}^{\infty } \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
